X.note: The globe render has good depth and an atmospheric rim, and the Texas highlight is clear. The callout is wide and sits on top of the Gulf and Louisiana, with a thin leader that barely connects to its pin. The text is small and the source line is tiny. The map is a static, stateless region with no route or movement, and the frame shows no 'stories' or building visual. The caption and callout say almost the same thing. The orange Texas fill looks muddy against the terrain.

Y.note: The frame is clean and uncluttered. The shaded-relief coastline is attractive and reads at once as a coast with an origin point (Ulsan). The lines fan out to endpoints, so the route concept is visible. Callouts are compact with good contrast. Weaknesses: the destination pins are unlabeled and anonymous, so 'abroad' stays vague, the ocean is a flat empty fill, the dashed lines look slightly generic, and the arrowheads and sense of scale are missing.

why: Y reads faster and is cleaner, with a clear origin and route, while X is a prettier globe but its wide callout is awkward and it shows no movement or route.
top_fix_for_weaker: Shrink the Texas callout into a compact two-line label placed over empty ocean, with a clear leader line. Zoom the camera in so Texas fills more of the frame. Raise the text size to at least about 28px. Cut the duplicated caption. Add a real visual of the six-story, single-stair building, such as a stacked-floor icon or a number overlay, so the key quantity shows on screen.
